_: INVENTED, PHOTO-SOURCED CONTENT — epoch 2024-2025. NEVER A SOURCE FOR ANY MEASURED CONSUMER. Every entity in this document is modelled from published architectural photography and a 2021 design site plan, not from OSM, not from LiDAR, and not from the ArcGIS survey. Positions are INFERRED: each item names the surveyed polygon it was anchored to (`anchor`), and that anchor is the only measured fact behind it. Nothing here may be read back as a measurement of the campus, quoted as a height, a colour or a position by campus-eighth.js, campus-eighth-furniture.js, the corridor builders, or any gate. It renders and it is labelled; it does not inform. Class rule: docs/js/campus-photo-eighth.js header, and the README's photo-sourced section.

keeling.label: Charles David Keeling Apartments — photo-sourced detail
keeling.epoch: photo 2011-2013 (KieranTimberlake / Tim Griffith; Spurlock Poirier / attention2), reconciled against Google satellite fetched 2026-08-04
keeling.note: INVENTED, PHOTO-SOURCED CONTENT. Every entity here is modelled from published architectural photography of a building completed in 2011, not from OSM, not from LiDAR and not from the ArcGIS survey. The measured world keeps deciding WHERE and HOW BIG: every facade layer names the measured ring and the two measured ring vertices it hangs off, and floats at most 1 m proud of that face. Nothing in this section may be read back as a measurement by any measured consumer.

grid.moduleNote: 3.60 m floor-to-floor and the 1.20 m parapet are DERIVED from the measured LiDAR heights (37.2 = 10x3.60+1.20; 30.0 = 8x3.60+1.20; 22.8 = 6x3.60+1.20, zero residual). The 1.20 m HORIZONTAL bay is photogrammetric and it is contested: two independent reads of the head-on elevation kt_keeling2.png give 1.18 m and 1.224 m (vertical scale pinned by the derived 3.60 m floor-to-floor), while autocorrelating the projecting-fin comb in the georeferenced satellite chunks — from directly above, over the full 48.9 m and 49.2 m south faces of both towers — gives a fundamental at 1.02 m with a strong harmonic at 2.03 m. 1.20 m is used because the elevation photograph measures the bay directly and twice; the satellite's 1.02 m is most consistent with the BALUSTRADE POST pitch, whose 2.03 m harmonic is then the fins at every second post. Flagged in absent.

The North Tower's north elevation is not photographed anywhere in the cached set. It is skinned System B by the single-loaded-corridor logic alone; its window rhythm and its stair-slot position are inferred, not sourced.

The horizontal facade module is unresolved between 1.20 m (two reads of the head-on elevation kt_keeling2.png) and 1.02 m (fin-comb autocorrelation over both towers' full south faces in the georeferenced satellite). 1.20 m is built; see grid.moduleNote.
The inner re-entrant corners where the bar meets the North Tower, and the notches in both tower rings, are skinned as flat faces — no photograph resolves how the two systems turn those corners.

The grating mesh pitch is not measured. The balustrade is built as a semi-transparent aggregate plane plus real bars at 0.30 m, tuned to read at the photographed openness, not to a sourced bar spacing.
The teal glass hex is estimated — every crop of a teal pane in the cached set is contaminated by reflected sky or by the wet-weather cast of ls_016.jpg.
Wet-weather staining. The dark vertical water-stain streaks below every panel's top edge in ls_016.jpg are a state, not a material, and the rest of the model is dry.
Night lighting. No night photograph of this building exists in any source reached; the luminaires are geometry only and emit nothing.

Trees. The measured LiDAR tree layer already owns the eucalyptus, the courtyard sycamores and the redbuds — the building is 2011 and the LiDAR is 2014, so they are in the survey. Nothing here plants anything.
The small red object standing in the courtyard paving at about (-167, 434) in the satellite, also visible in c6_towerB.png — roughly 1.7 m square and unidentifiable at any available resolution.

Building-number graphics. The painted numeral '3' on the South Tower's undercroft wall is legible in ls_016.jpg, but no other number is, and one number without the set would be a false claim about which building is which.

galbraith.label: Galbraith Hall, Revelle College — photo-sourced detail
galbraith.note: INVENTED class. Deems Lewis Martin, 1965; Kevin deFreitas Architects renovation 2013. Every dimension here comes from a dated photograph or from the architect's Second Floor Plan, scaled against the MEASURED ring in campus-3d.json and the MEASURED LiDAR height. Nothing measured reads back from this section.
galbraith.colorNote: Hexes are pixel medians with the lighting condition named. Two are adjusted from the raw sample and say so: pavingBuff is the ucsdmap.jpg median desaturated for that frame's overcast warm cast, and cofferPan/soffitRib sit mid-way between the sunlit-bounce and deep-shade samples because the renderer supplies its own shading.

measured.heightNote: The 2014 LiDAR ground is FLAT at 23.6 m over the whole footprint and for 40 m on every side of it (sampled on a 2 m grid). There is no storey-high step between the north plaza and the south lawn, so the survey's earlier reading — LiDAR 16.6 above the lawn, ArcGIS 12.8 above a plaza one storey higher — cannot be what these two numbers are. On flat ground, LiDAR 16.6 is simply the roof above grade on all four sides, and this section puts its eaves exactly there, on top of the measured mass, so nothing measured is left standing above the roof. How the 16.6 divides is read off oceanlight-21220.jpg, which is near-orthographic: scaling that elevation so grade-to-roof is 16.6 gives a 5.6 m lower glazed band, a 3.2 m terrace zone, a 4.5 m upper glazed band and a 3.2 m roof edge — two levels of about 7.4 m and a slab of about 1.8, which sums back to 16.6 with no residual. Two glazed bands split by one mid-level balcony is what the north, south and west photographs all show, and a 7.4 m level is corroborated on the north by ad01-entry-before.jpg, where the plaza-level glazing stands about three door-heights tall. LiDAR decides the ground and the top; the photographs decide only how the space between them divides.
measured.conflict: UNRESOLVED, two ways. ArcGIS says 3 levels and only 2 are expressed on any photographed elevation; the third is taken to be internal (the plan sheets describe a 417-seat lecture hall and a mezzanine) and nothing is built for it. ArcGIS also says 12.8 m against LiDAR's 16.6, and on flat ground nothing accounts for the 3.8 m difference — the roof monitors are the likeliest explanation and they cannot be confirmed, so LiDAR is followed and the discrepancy is left standing rather than modelled around.

grid.datumNote: standoff, roofOut and every facade projection are measured from the GLAZING PLANE, not from the measured ring: 3.4 m is what the photographs read between the glass and the strut line, and it has to stay 3.4 m however far out the glazing itself has to hang to clear the drawn mass.
grid.calibration: The architect's plan gives 10.83 m between pair centres. That number was calibrated against a 45.8 m enclosed block, and it does NOT survive contact with the surveyed 62 m footprint: the measured ring is the wall this section is allowed to hang on, and five pairs at 10.83 m only span 45.8 m of it. So the drawing's SPACING is dropped and its COUNT is kept — five pairs, 2.45 m inside a pair, both of which are independently countable in oceanlight-21220.jpg — spread across the measured face. The measured world decides scale; the photographs decide what is on it.
grid.moduleNote: The coffer module survives that, because it is corroborated twice over: it is the drawing's own pair spacing over eight (10.83 / 8 = 1.354), and it is also the size that puts the 46 coffers counted across the elevation onto the 62 m measured face (62.0 / 46 = 1.348). The two agree to 6 mm. The oversail is six of them, counted in ad01-entry-before.jpg and again in wm-from-below.jpg.
grid.source: ad-plan-L2.jpg, Kevin deFreitas Architects Second Floor Plan, 02.17.12

column.profileNote: Half-widths are the LATHE CIRCUMRADIUS of a four-sided section, so what an elevation actually shows is radius x sqrt(2): a 0.83 head reads as the photographed 1.17 m bracket and the 0.38 waist as a 0.54 m shaft. Not a straight box and not a plain taper: thin at the waist, sweeping out below into a wide flat foot and flaring above into a broad bracket that meets the beam hard. Section is square with the diagonal facing the wall, which is what ad01 and ucsdmap both show.

roofEdge.source: crop-roofedge.jpg (2011) and wm-from-below.jpg (2026) — present in both epochs

facade.wallStandoffNote: Not a style choice. campus-massing.js extrudes the UNIVERSITY'S massing ring, which stands up to 0.799 m outside the OSM ring this section is anchored to. Glazing hung any closer than that disappears inside the drawn box on the east elevation. The standoff is that clearance plus 0.15 m and nothing more.
facade.mullionNote: ESTIMATE, 1.5-1.8 m read off ad01; finer than the coffer module, never equal to it.

entry.beamNote: The two beams ride the middle pair's column lines and carry the 'Galbraith Hall' lettering on their outer fascia. The lettering itself is ABSENT: there is no text mechanism in this renderer and a painted-on rectangle would be worse than nothing.
entry.signNote: The 'Theatre & Dance Department' hanging blade, in both wm-from-below and flickr.

west.gradeNote: The 2014 ground rises 3.2 m from x -8 to a ridge at x -16.5 that runs dead straight for the whole length of the west face. That ridge is what the lava wall in ucsdmap.jpg retains, but it is also exactly the shape a bare-earth classifier leaves along a hedge or a wall line, so nothing here asserts it is topography: the wall is placed at its crest, OUTSIDE the roof, and every solid on this side is seated per-item on the drawn surface rather than on a level.

absent: Roof monitors — the shallow segmental barrel vaults are confirmed from INSIDE only (ad-2012-194.jpg). No aerial or rooftop photograph of Galbraith was found, so their count, spacing, orientation and cladding are all unknown. Flat deck, monitors unbuilt.
All rooftop plant, ducts, screens and stair overruns — same reason: no source sees the roof.

The entire east ground plane. No photograph of the east elevation toward Blake Hall exists. The east face gets the colonnade, glazing and roof edge it must share with the other three, and nothing else; no paving, planting, steps or furniture is claimed there.
Bike racks, light poles, bollards and wayfinding signage anywhere around the building — visible as smudges in ucsdmap.jpg, never resolved.
The dark collar at some column bases in ucsdmap.jpg — unresolved between paint, shadow and a leaning object.
The 'Galbraith Hall' and 'Theatre & Dance Department' lettering. The blades that carry it are built; the glyphs are not, because this renderer has no text mechanism.
The pre-2013 CLICS teal sign (#61838d, gold lettering) — a dead epoch, superseded by the red entry canopy.
The green metal picnic table and the coral tree east of the west court in ucsdmap.jpg — too coarse in the only frame that holds them.
The La Jolla Project granite blocks on the south lawn — already built by campus-landmarks.json, and never duplicated here.
Interior fitout of every level, including the 417-seat lecture hall the plan sheets describe.
